content.text:
This Outlook Scheduling Assistant screenshot shows the free/busy times of six attendees and the room NYC-12 Hudson (8) on Monday and Tuesday (all times New York time). I need to book a 60-minute meeting. Rules: Priya Shah and Marcus Lee are required; at least 2 of the other four (Elena Ruiz, Kenji Watanabe, Grace Liu and Jamal Wright) must also be able to attend; tentative (hatched) blocks count as free, while busy and out-of-office blocks count as busy; the meeting must not overlap the 12:00-13:00 lunch hour; the room row must be free for the whole meeting; the meeting must lie within 9:00-17:00 and start on a quarter hour. What is the earliest start time that satisfies every rule? Answer as the day and the 24-hour start time, in the form `Tue 09:45` (three-letter day, HH:MM with a leading zero).

Think step by step. Then end your reply with one final line in exactly this form:
FINAL ANSWER: <your answer>

message.content:
On Monday, the earliest required-attendee and room opening is 16:00–17:00, but only Jamal is available among the four optional attendees for that full hour. So Monday has no valid slot.

On Tuesday, the pre-lunch opening at 11:15 would overlap lunch, and the room and Priya’s busy time rule out earlier post-lunch starts. At 15:15, Priya and Marcus are available, the room is free, and Grace and Jamal can attend; the meeting ends at 16:15.

FINAL ANSWER: Tue 15:15
